support.cpu_lane_types_note: The routed experts of a qwen4exp file are computed here when they do not fit in VRAM. An expert whose gate/up/down type is outside this set cannot leave the GPU. qwen35moe has NO tiering at all -- its experts must be resident.
support.batched_prefill: qwen35moe and qwen35: eligible when the geometry and F32 router allow (boot prints `prefill planes 2, chunk 1024 tokens`). qwen4exp: OFF unconditionally -- `I.pf_able = able && !q4e` (src/cuda/gpu.cu:486), the batched int8 path has no hyper-connection / PLE recipe, so rung 3 prefill runs through the 8-row verify window.

models.measured: with the dense 27B as the target (--ctx 4096, greedy, 200 tokens): decode 39.5-39.9 tok/s, `spec 199/56 (3.49 tokens a pass, 142 of 174 drafts kept)`, dflash 56 cycles. The same 27B with MTP alone measured 32.7 tok/s on the same box -- so the drafter is +21% and 84% of its drafts are kept. Boot: `dflash ... matrices in q8, one pass drafts up to 7 tokens (10.3 ms; plain row 52.4 ms), a context of 2,048 positions a slot; chosen per cycle by tokens per ms, k by the drafts' own confidence`. VRAM 1.88 GiB.
models.combine_verified: `--spec auto` prints `speculation MTP + ngram (n 8, up to 7) + DFlash2` and the per-cycle log then reads `mtp 0 cycles, ngram 1 cycles 0 of 4 kept, dflash 56 cycles 142 of 170 kept`: all three sources are offered every cycle, each is scored as expected tokens per ms with its own acceptance EMA, and the picker takes the winner. dflash wins on this content and the other two cost nothing. Decode is identical to `--spec dflash` (39.9), which is the point -- the picker is source-agnostic.
models.blocker: was `--draft-model <path>: no readable model.safetensors (and config.json) there` (Dflash::load took safetensors only). FIXED: Dflash::load now has a GGUF branch, and its two callers were fixed with it -- Dflash::estimate (which gpu_backend.cu:106 uses to decide whether the drafter fits, and returned 0 for a GGUF, so the engine refused before it ever tried to load).
models.notes: The LOADER has no GGUF path: Dflash::load accepts only a path ending .safetensors, or a DIRECTORY holding model.safetensors + config.json with a dflash_config section (src/cuda/dflash.cu:493-507). No safetensors drafter exists anywhere in the local HF cache, so --spec dflash is unreachable for that reason alone. EVERYTHING ELSE THE BRANCH NEEDS IS IN THE FILE -- the GGUF carries the whole dflash_config as metadata, so there is no research left, only transcription.

gguf_config._note: these map 1:1 onto the DflashConfig fields the safetensors branch reads out of config.json's dflash_config + top level (src/cuda/dflash.cu:514-538), and the file also ships the tokenizer (gpt2/qwen35) and a base_model pointer to Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.

gguf_tensor_map._note: GGUF from the safetensors checkpoint: every name below is `blk.<N>.<role>` in the file, except the five globals. Left = the role name, right = the safetensors name Dflash::load asks for (src/cuda/dflash.cu:596-604 and after). 21 roles, 81 tensors: 5 per-layer roles x 5 layers plus the globals.
gguf_tensor_map.fc.weight: fc.weight  [5*5120 x 5120] -- the input projection from the target's stacked layer outputs

what_the_branch_must_do: 1. Detect the file by magic/extension and read the geometry from dflash.* instead of config.json (table above) -- no config.json exists beside a GGUF.

2. Replace the `st::Tensor` accessor with a small handle that can be either backend, carrying dtype, n_elements, nbytes and a to_f32() -- because the GGUF is Q6_K and Q6_K is not a dtype Dflash::load accepts today (`tensor ... is BF16` is a hard requirement at src/cuda/dflash.cu:562-565).

3. Decode Q6_K with quants::dequant_row(type, src, dst, n) (include/limbo/quants.hpp:103, already implemented and parity-tested) and then feed the EXISTING encoders: quants::quantize_q8_0 for --draft-quant q8, or a bf16 repack for the default. The upload loop at src/cuda/dflash.cu:646-666 is where that goes.

4. The two selector codebooks live in mapped host memory (cudaHostAllocMapped, src/cuda/dflash.cu:672-681) and are read 32 rows at a time; decode them to bf16 once at load, as the norm vectors already do.
5. Scope: 81 tensors, one file, no new kernels and no new numerics -- every decoder and encoder it needs is already in the tree and parity-tested against ggml.

verdict.summary: Three rungs of the ladder run, and the first two of them run WELL: rung 1 fits the card with MTP and a batched prefill at chunk 1024, the dense 27B fits easily with a real nextn block at blk.64, and rung 3 runs in its q4e shape. Rung 2 is refused purely on residency and is the only model that would exercise the expert tiers -- and the tiers do not exist for its architecture. The prior version of this file said the ladder was not on this box; that was wrong, and the cause was a find with maxdepth 6 against snapshot paths seven deep.
